title: Weekly upstream drift routine: new usd-core/OpenUSD release -> run suite -> email
description: First weft routine (founder 2026-11-07). Weekly cloud routine: check PyPI usd-core and OpenUSD GitHub releases newer than last seen; install the newest usd-core in a venv, run the full suite plus the schema regeneration diff; email the maintainer only on a new release (pass or fail) or a failure. Built on the support digest kit shape from Kilroy (collect, triage, render, mail adapter, state); it is the first real test of the shared-core boundary (Kilroy bead SkyPainterBuild-ft5f.7). Routine gets an explicit connector list (Gmail only) and no repo writes.
acceptance_criteria: A dry run emails the current newest usd-core version and the suite result; a second run with no new release sends nothing.

title: Push the 3 local-only main commits (prim-threads spec + plan, ignore .claude/worktrees) through a PR
description: Found 2026-11-07: the main checkout's main is 3 commits ahead of origin/main (c16b284, 6e672b4, 119b3ad). Move them to a branch, PR, merge, then reset local main to origin/main so it stops diverging.
acceptance_criteria: origin/main contains the 3 commits via a merged PR and local main equals origin/main.
close_reason: Acceptance: origin/main contains the 3 commits and local main equals origin/main. Met: yes, no PR needed. The premise was wrong: c16b284, 6e672b4 and 119b3ad were already on origin/main; local main was 171 commits BEHIND (stale origin ref misread as ahead). Fast-forwarded local main to origin/main 31b4a8d on 2026-11-07; git status clean.

title: Bring the swarm-eval review and thread-viewer spec into main
description: Two docs lived only on side branches: claude/agent-swarm-eval-f9xgct (docs/reviews/2026-09-04-swarm-eval/, 9 files) and local weft-viewer (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-thread-viewer-design.md). Founder 2026-11-07: keep them. Same PR carries the pending beads export.

title: GitHub Issues intake: convert real user reports to beads
description: Beads is the work tracker; GitHub Issues is the public intake. When a user issue is real (reproduces, or 2+ people), create a bead that links the issue URL and reference the bead in a reply. Later a digest routine can do the conversion automatically.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md documents the intake rule and the first real user issue has a linked bead.
